summary.title: Sell Yourself Sell Your Work
summary.one_liner: Doing great technical work is not enough; you must write about it and communicate it clearly so the wider world can benefit from it.
keywords: richard hamming you and your research
takeaways: Excellent work that is never communicated is effectively wasted, both for the world and for your own benefit.
Technical people often skip writing reports because they consider it boring or irrelevant, but clear writing saves others time and builds reputation.
Presentation matters: spelling, punctuation and clear purpose affect whether readers take your work seriously.
For a company, the work's value is only realised when it is sold; 'selling' means getting known, not just making a product.
Richard W. Hamming's talk 'You and Your Research' is cited for a fuller discussion of what 'sell' means.
summary.summary: This short essay from the solipsys.co.uk blog argues that technically excellent work only benefits the world and its author if it is written up and communicated well. The author observes that many talented engineers avoid report writing, and notes that entrepreneurs must sell their products to survive. The piece briefly references Richard W. Hamming's 1986 talk "You and Your Research" to explain that "sell" has a broader meaning. The page also contains site navigation and a list of the author's other blog posts, which are not summarised here.
